what: The risky-test uplift domain: a provider-proposed test that exercises a REAL external tool (ffmpeg, LabVIEW's CLI) that hosted CI cannot provide. Tool-gated acceptance: SKIP when the tool is absent, run + gate when present.

cases.present-pass: tool=node (always present) + a passing test -> verdict=pass (risky-test-runs ok)
cases.absent-skip: an absent required tool -> verdict=SKIP (not fail); a skipped check is recorded
cases.present-fail: tool present + a failing test -> verdict=fail

ffmpeg.ollamaProposed: verdict=fail -- llama3.1:8b wrote CommonJS require('child_process') in an ESM .mjs (require is not defined) -> the test threw -> the gate correctly FAILED it (teeth)
ffmpeg.correctTest: verdict=pass -- a correct ESM `ffmpeg -version` test ran the real /usr/bin/ffmpeg (tool-present:ffmpeg ok, risky-test-runs ok, exit 0)

labview.installed: /usr/local/natinst/LabVIEW-2026-64 (present on disk, UNACTIVATED, CLI not on PATH)
labview.result: tool=labviewcli -> present:false -> verdict=SKIP -- the risky test correctly skips where the CLI is not runnable

safety: The risky-test executes a provider-proposed test that invokes a real tool. The DETERMINISTIC gate uses node itself as the always-present tool (safe). UNTRUSTED provider-proposed tests that drive ffmpeg/LabVIEW run in the DISPOSABLE cleanroom VM -- exactly where the Ollama ffmpeg test above executed -- not on a trusted host.
note: The same domain gate is a deterministic no-op (skip) under the dependency-free CI suite (no ffmpeg/LabVIEW) and a real proof in the cleanroom. LabVIEW activation is an operator-only step; an activated + PATH-exposed LabVIEWCLI flips the LabVIEW case from skip to a real run.
